Global Relief, Bitcoin Rallies
Bitcoin rose nearly 3% on Wednesday, renewing Friday's high (
) and reaching
at the day's peak. Volume came in above the seven-day average, showing genuine participation in the upward move.

The catalyst was Trump's announcement of an expanded ceasefire between the US and Iran, which triggered risk appetite across global markets. The Nasdaq gained 2.67% and the S&P 500 advanced 1.64%. Gold fell 2.35% and silver dropped 5.43%, confirming capital rotation out of safe-haven assets into risk assets.
The $73,000 support held firm across four recent tests, and the geopolitical narrative supported the rally.
The price is now approaching a key barrier in the $80,000 range.

Beyond $80,000
The bullish scenario confirms if Bitcoin breaks
with sustained volume and closes the day above that level. Today's high came within less than 1% of that barrier, and buying activity picked up alongside geopolitical optimism.

The catalysts supporting this possibility are the continuation of US-Iran diplomatic relief, positive institutional flows (Strategy continues buying aggressively), and the derivatives setup. The long-to-short ratio in futures stands at 0.51, meaning for every long position there are nearly two shorts, creating conditions for a rapid short squeeze.
If confirmed,
the first target is the $82,000 range

, in the 100-week EMA zone.
If Optimism Cools
The bearish scenario activates if Bitcoin is rejected in the $80,000 range and loses support at
, which corresponds to Wednesday's low. A rejection at that level would bring the price back toward consolidated support.
The first downside target would be
, the consolidated support. If that level is lost, the next relevant floor sits in the
range. A daily close above $80,000 would invalidate this scenario.

Risks include a reversal of the diplomatic backdrop with renewed US-Iran tensions and negative surprises in US economic data. There is also on-chain fragility reported in the $78,000–$73,000 range, where buyer support is thin.
Thursday Radar
The key level to watch over the next few hours is the

barrier. A breakout with strong volume could trigger a liquidation cascade of short positions and accelerate the rally. A rejection could open the door to position closing after a five-day sequence of higher lows.

Market sentiment improved rapidly, with Fear & Greed jumping to 46, still in fear territory. US markets operate normally tomorrow, and the continuation of the move will depend on how price reacts in that range.
